Hi Evelyn,

We're asking Redwood to execute a full purge for the Helix project (customer id HS-4721) across the eu-central-1 deployment. Scope: all prompt inputs, generated outputs, KV cache entries, and request/response access logs tied to the Helix environment (helix-prod-eu & helix-staging-eu).

Regulatory context: HealthStack has received a data subject request and also wants evidence for internal audit. Can you confirm:
- The exact operations you will run (components and artifacts removed)
- Expected timeline from acknowledgment to proof delivery
- The form of proof (S3 manifest + checksums, drive link with redaction snapshots, or signed attestation)

Hi Marta — thanks for the details and the heads-up. We can handle this. Quick answers up-front:

1) Operations we'll run
- Prompt/output sweep: enumerate prompt-output objects for Helix (by project tag HS-4721), soft-delete then hard-delete following our erase-playbook.
- KV cache eviction: clear model KV caches associated with helix-prod-eu to remove any cached prompt state.
- Access/log purge: remove request/response logs older than the retention window and explicit Helix-related log objects; where logs are immutable (audit systems), we'll provide a signed attestation and an exported manifest.

2) Timeline
- Acknowledgement: now.
- Execution window: targeted within 48 hours for full sweep; smaller batches may complete sooner.
- Proof delivery: secure Drive link + CSV manifest within 4 business days (or earlier depending on scoped object count).

3) Proof formats
- CSV manifest (object id, path, deletion timestamp, operator id)
- Drive folder with redaction snapshots for records that require human review
- Optional signed attestation issued by Redwood compliance on request

4) Side effects
- There should be no customer-facing downtime; KV eviction may temporarily increase token-generation latency for warm-model requests.
- We'll coordinate with you if we detect risk of degraded performance.

Action items for HealthStack: please confirm the exact project tags/environments to scope (we've assumed helix-prod-eu and helix-staging-eu) and whether Shield Compliance (emma@shieldcompliance.io) should be copied on the final evidence.

I've attached our eradication checklist to this email and CC'd Marissa and Ben to start the execution once you confirm scope.

Attachments: eradication-checklist.csv

Regards,
Evelyn Hart

Hi Marta / HealthStack team —

Execution complete for the scope provided (helix-prod-eu; helix-staging-eu). Summary below and proof links attached.

What we removed
- 1,230 prompt-output objects (soft-delete + hard-delete cycles completed)
- 48 KV cache keys evicted and garbage-collected
- 2,870 request/response log objects identified as Helix-related: where logs were mutable they were deleted; where logs are committed to immutable audit stores we produced an export manifest and a signed attestation.

Proof delivered
- Drive folder (redwood evidence): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-Helix-Evidence
- CSV manifest (deleted_objects.csv) listing ids, internal paths, deletion timestamp (UTC), and operator id
- deletion-evidence-20280514.zip (contains manifest + redaction snapshots + operator run-log)

Notes on verification and next steps
- All items were removed from our active stores and caches; a final scrubbing job will run in 7 days to remove any remainders in tiered object storage (this is standard for our cold-tier lifecycle). We included the cold-tier manifest in the ZIP.
- If you require a signed compliance attestation, Priya (CC) can prepare a formal statement on Redwood letterhead.
- Suggested improvement: we can configure a Helix account-level scheduled purge (monthly/quarterly) and an automated evidence export if HealthStack wants ongoing self-service.

Attachments: deletion-evidence-20280514.zip, eradication-checklist.csv
